subject: springboot
question: Which starter brings in Spring MVC with an embedded Tomcat server?
explanation: spring-boot-starter-web includes Spring MVC and spring-boot-starter-tomcat; webflux uses Reactor Netty by default.

subject: springboot
question: What is a Spring Boot starter such as spring-boot-starter-data-jpa?
options: A dependency descriptor that pulls in a curated set of libraries for a feature
A Maven plugin that generates the main application class
A Java agent that instruments beans at runtime
A CLI command that scaffolds a new project
explanation: Starters are convenience dependencies that aggregate compatible libraries so you do not manage them individually.

subject: springboot
question: Which simple setting makes Spring Boot print the condition evaluation report showing which auto-configurations matched?
explanation: Starting the app with debug=true (or --debug) logs the conditions report listing positive and negative auto-configuration matches.

subject: springboot
question: How can you disable one specific auto-configuration class such as DataSourceAutoConfiguration?
explanation: The exclude attribute of @SpringBootApplication (or @EnableAutoConfiguration) prevents that auto-configuration from being applied.

subject: springboot
question: In Spring Boot 3, where are auto-configuration classes registered in a library jar?
explanation: Boot 3 removed support for registering auto-configurations in spring.factories; the AutoConfiguration.imports file is used instead.

subject: springboot
question: Which annotation, introduced in Spring Boot 2.7, marks a class as an auto-configuration?
explanation: @AutoConfiguration is a specialized @Configuration with proxyBeanMethods=false and before/after ordering attributes.

subject: springboot
question: When does an auto-configuration annotated with @ConditionalOnClass(DataSource.class) apply?
options: Only when a DataSource bean is already defined
Only when the class is annotated with @Entity
Only when DataSource is present on the classpath
explanation: @ConditionalOnClass checks classpath presence, which is how starters trigger configuration just by being added.

subject: springboot
question: What does @ConditionalOnMissingBean on an auto-configured @Bean method achieve?
options: The default bean backs off if the application already defines a bean of that type
The bean is created lazily on first injection
The bean is created only if no other configuration class exists
The bean replaces any user-defined bean of that type
explanation: This is how auto-configuration lets user-defined beans override Boot's defaults.

subject: springboot
question: Why is @ConditionalOnMissingBean reliable in auto-configurations but risky in ordinary user @Configuration classes?
options: It is evaluated against beans registered so far, and auto-configurations are processed after user configuration
User configuration classes ignore all conditions
It is evaluated lazily at first injection only in auto-configurations
Auto-configurations are processed in a separate child context
explanation: Condition evaluation depends on registration order; auto-configurations run after user beans are defined, so they see them.

subject: springboot
question: What does @AutoConfiguration(after = DataSourceAutoConfiguration.class) control?
options: That it is only applied when DataSourceAutoConfiguration is excluded
That its beans are created after the application has started
That this auto-configuration is processed after DataSourceAutoConfiguration
explanation: Ordering ensures conditions like @ConditionalOnBean(DataSource.class) can see beans from the referenced auto-configuration.

subject: springboot
question: A bean has @ConditionalOnProperty(name = "feature.cache.enabled", havingValue = "true") with matchIfMissing left at its default. The property is absent. What happens?
options: The bean is created lazily on first use
The bean is created because missing properties default to true
Startup fails with a missing property error
The condition does not match and the bean is not created
explanation: matchIfMissing defaults to false, so an absent property means the condition fails.

subject: springboot
question: Which Spring Boot utility is designed for testing an auto-configuration's conditions without starting the full application?
explanation: ApplicationContextRunner lets you add configurations and properties and assert on the resulting context quickly.
